items.title: Antonelli leads the extended Qatar FP2
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli set 1:23.077, 0.127 seconds ahead of George Russell; Lando Norris was third at +0.445s. The FIA Document 21 table matches Formula1.com across all 22 classified drivers. Two red flags interrupted the session, which was extended by 13 minutes. A Virtual Safety Car followed when Hamilton stopped after reporting lost power.
items.why_it_matters: The official report does not establish a cause for Hamilton's loss of power. The interrupted session is not a long-run comparison.

items.title: FIA fines Audi €500 for Hülkenberg pit-lane speeding
items.summary: Document 20 records Car 27 at 84.4 km/h in the 80 km/h pit lane during FP2. The €500 fine is imposed on Audi Revolut F1 Team, not the driver.
items.why_it_matters: This is a team fine, not a grid penalty or sporting penalty for Hülkenberg.

items.title: Norris sees Mercedes well clear after Friday practice
items.summary: After Mercedes led both Friday sessions, Lando Norris said McLaren may be fighting for P3 and estimated it was roughly 0.6–0.7 seconds per lap off Mercedes. McLaren ran an older floor on Friday and plans to use its newer specification on Saturday; the team expects a modest, not transformative, gain.
items.why_it_matters: Norris’s gap estimate is a Friday assessment, not a qualifying result. Check whether the new floor narrows the margin and how McLaren compares with Red Bull and Ferrari.

sources.label: Formula1.com Norris and McLaren Friday assessment

items.title: Qatar pre-weekend tyre-set totals remain inconsistent
items.summary: Formula1.com’s preview lists 2/3/8 sets with an extra Soft reserved for Q3, while its explainer lists 2/4/7. Pirelli confirms C1/C2/C3 and the 27-lap limit, but neither source resolves the totals or reports remaining sets. The later FIA Document 25 reports scrutineering checks, not per-driver tyre inventory or a new pressure table.
items.why_it_matters: Keep both allocations attributed; use neither as remaining sets or as a race-strategy inventory. The latest pressure values are not a post-FP2 reaffirmation.

items.title: Gasly explains high-speed FP2 spin and floor damage
items.summary: Gasly said an earlier red flag left his tyres cooler than expected; he described lower pressures, increased bottoming and a spin that brought out another red flag. He reported floor damage and said the team would repair it for Saturday.
items.why_it_matters: This is Gasly’s account of the incident, not a confirmed mechanical fault. Alpine’s managing director also described the car as difficult to handle and did not attribute the spin solely to driver error.

sources.label: Formula1.com Gasly on his FP2 spin
